prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthContext loses `token_expiry_time` when tokens are loaded from storage on init/restart, so `is_token_valid()` treats an already-expired stored token as valid and the proactive pre-request refresh is skipped, forcing an unnecessary interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthContext loses `token_expiry_time` when tokens are loaded from storage on init/restart, so `is_token_valid()` treats an already-expired stored token as valid and the proactive pre-request refresh is skipped, forcing an unnecessary interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 1784 fixes the root cause directly at the source in `_initialize` by calling `context.update_token_expiry()` on stored tokens whenever `expires_in` is present - a 4-line change that reuses the same expiry-computation path already used for freshly-issued tokens, and it ships a dedicated `expired_tokens` fixture/test. 2875's own inline comment attributes its need to this exact same bug ("A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time"), but instead of fixing it at load time it adds a ~15-line fallback branch inside the 401 handler of `async_auth_flow` that attempts a silent refresh before falling back to full re-auth. prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection in `_handle_reconnection` exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the original request's caller was previously left hanging forever with no response and no exception (the exceeded-attempts branch just logged and returned). (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same `if attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` branch in `_handle_reconnection`, but #2395's fix is the narrower, more surgical change: it sends a JSONRPCError keyed to `ctx.session_message.message.id` through the existing `read_stream_writer`, resolving only the specific pending request while leaving the rest of the session/connection intact, and it also upgrades the log line from debug to warning and removes the prior `# pragma: no cover` (indicating the branch is now actually exercised by a test). #3098 instead raises a `StreamableHTTPError` out of the task group and adds a new recursive `_unwrap_exception` helper just to dig that error back out of a `BaseExceptionGroup` — a hard-failure approach that would tear down the whole client connection on any reconnection failure rather than just the affected request, and it also touches unrelated code (reverting the `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` alias), widening its diff and merge-conflict surface without addressing anything #2395 doesn't already cover.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the full header into scheme-delimited segments first (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then scopes extraction to the segments belonging to the Bearer scheme specifically (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips everything after the first space in the whole header and comma-splits that remainder, with no scheme-boundary check, so it would misattribute params from a second challenge (e.g. a trailing Bearer challenge after a Basic one) to the same token list. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the underlying substring/boundary-matching bug; #3012 should be closed in favor of it.

clusters.pick_reason: 3263 fixes cold-start refresh for every TokenStorage backend by re-running discovery before the refresh attempt when metadata is missing, tracking `eager_discovery_attempted` to avoid repeated blind probes on subsequent in-process refreshes, and adds an issuer-binding check against the rediscovered metadata to guard against metadata mix-up. 2492 instead adds new optional `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the TokenStorage protocol that default to a no-op, so any storage implementation that doesn't add the new methods (the common case for existing consumers) remains broken with no fix applied, and it includes no equivalent of the issuer verification 3263 performs.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the exact same block in validate_tool_use_result_messages that mis-fires when an assistant tool_use message is not followed by any tool_result: the pre-existing code computed tool_result_ids as an empty set in that case and compared it to non-empty tool_use_ids, raising 'ids do not match'. The two PRs reach opposite conclusions about the correct fix: #2962 adds a `has_tool_results` guard so the whole mismatch check (and any error) is skipped when there are no tool_results at all, citing SEP-1577 that a tool_use need not be followed by a tool_result, with a regression test asserting no exception is raised. #3053 instead adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` so the same scenario still raises, just with a clearer message, with a test asserting an exception IS raised. Since both edit the identical lines for the identical triggering scenario but assert mutually exclusive expected behavior (no-raise vs. raise-with-clearer-message), only one can be merged. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 splits the full header into scheme-delimited segments first (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then scopes extraction to the segments belonging to the Bearer scheme specifically (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips everything after the first space in the whole header and comma-splits that remainder, with no scheme-boundary check, so it would misattribute params from a second challenge (e.g. a trailing Bearer challenge after a Basic one) to the same token list. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the underlying substring/boundary-matching bug; #3012 should be closed in favor of it.
